content.problemStatement:
You receive `n` pairs of parentheses. Generate all combinations of well-formed (balanced) parentheses using exactly `n` pairs. Output the list of distinct valid strings. The order of strings in the returned list does not matter.

A string of parentheses is well-formed if every opening parenthesis has a matching closing parenthesis and pairs are properly nested. As an example, for `n = 3` the valid combinations are `"((()))","(()())","(())()","()(())","()()()"`.

Aim for an algorithm that runs in time proportional to the number of valid combinations (Catalan number) and uses O(n) auxiliary space for recursion/stack (excluding the output list).
constraints: Expected time complexity: O(Catalan(n) * n) where Catalan(n) is the number of valid combinations
Expected auxiliary space: O(n) (recursion / construction buffer) excluding output
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [n]. Example: [3]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised list of strings (order does not matter). Example: ["((()))","(()())","(())()","()(())","()()()"]
notes: Return all distinct well-formed parentheses strings that use exactly n pairs.
Order of strings in the output does not matter; the judge compares the returned set of strings (not sequence order).
Preferred approach: backtracking (build string while tracking remaining opens and closes), or dynamic programming that composes smaller results.
Do not attempt to generate invalid strings and filter them — build only valid prefixes to keep complexity optimal.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Only one valid combination for n = 1.

hidden.label: Regression: ensure no invalid strings produced
Sanity: ensure correct count for n=3 (5 strings)
Sanity: ensure correct count for n=2 (2 strings)
Sanity: ensure correct count for n=5 (42 strings) - representative full set

solution.approach: Backtracking (optimal for this problem): build strings incrementally, keeping counts of how many '(' and ')' have been used. At each step, you may add '(' if open_count < n, and you may add ')' if close_count < open_count. When the constructed string reaches length 2*n, add it to the result. This generates only valid strings and runs in O(Catalan(n) * n) time (each string of length 2n is constructed once) and uses O(n) recursion depth.
solution.timeComplexity: O(Catalan(n) * n) where Catalan(n) is the number of valid combinations
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary (recursion / construction buffer) plus output size
